title: Wrap-boundary collision remains open: the content backstop cannot fire, because the colliding state leaves the cursor row blank
description:
Follow-up to CAM-359 (shipped). CAM-359 replaced the content-matching submission oracle with cursor geometry and added `composerLineRetainsPayloadTail` as a backstop for the exact-wrap-boundary residue class. Round-2 review then correctly made that backstop read through a dedicated visible-screen reader. The backstop is nonetheless INERT for the case it exists to close, and the module header at src/tmux/dispatch.ts consequently OVERCLAIMS ('closes that residual gap').

MEASURED EVIDENCE (real claude Ink TUI v2.1.215, tmux pane 80x30, orchestrator probe 2026-07-20, not inferred).

Baseline, empty composer: cursor = (2,26).

Sweep of single-token (character-wrapping) payloads: no length collides. Wrap is LAZY: len=76 leaves the cursor parked at x=78 on the full row; len=77 moves to the continuation row at x=3. The cursor never rests at x=2 with text present, because a character placed on a continuation row puts the cursor at x=3.

  len=74 -> (76,26)   len=76 -> (78,26)   len=77 -> (3,26)   len=153 -> (3,26)

BUT the collision IS reachable when the payload ENDS IN A SPACE that lands on the boundary, because Ink word-wraps the trailing space onto the next row:

  len=75 trailing-space -> (77,26)
  len=76 trailing-space -> (78,26)
  len=77 trailing-space -> (2,26)   <-- IDENTICAL TO THE EMPTY BASELINE
  len=78 trailing-space -> (5,26)

So the collision is real (the round-1 CRITICAL was right), but it occurs ONLY in the trailing-space-at-boundary case.

WHY THE BACKSTOP CANNOT FIRE. In precisely that colliding state the cursor row is BLANK, and the payload tail lives on the row ABOVE:

  row[24] = '----------------------------------------' (composer top border)
  row[25] = '# word word word ... word w'              (payload text + prompt glyph)
  row[26] = ''                                          (cursor rests here, (2,26))
  row[27] = '----------------------------------------' (composer bottom border)

`composerLineRetainsPayloadTail` does `lines[cursorY]` -> '' -> `trimmed.length === 0` -> returns false -> geometry reads unchanged -> verdict DELIVERED. The undelivered payload is silently lost: the original CAM-358 defect, surviving for this residue class. The function's doc comment ('the trailing suffix ... is always CONTIGUOUS on the single row the cursor rests on') is false exactly at the collision. This is structural, not a tuning problem: whenever the geometry collides, the cursor row is whitespace-only BY CONSTRUCTION, so no tail-matching rule keyed on the cursor row can ever detect it.

PROPOSED FIX (exact, not probabilistic). When the geometry pair reads unchanged, discriminate on WHERE THE PROMPT GLYPH IS. An empty composer has the prompt on the cursor row itself; the colliding state has the cursor row blank with the prompt one row up alongside the payload:

  empty:     row[cursorY] = '# Try "how does <filepath> work?"'   (prompt on the cursor row)
  collision: row[cursorY] = ''                                     (blank; prompt at cursorY-1)

So 'the cursor row does not carry the prompt glyph' is a sound, exact 'still composing' signal. It needs no payload-derived matching at all, which also retires MIN_PAYLOAD_TAIL_MATCH and the suffix-length scan (round 2 SUGGESTION: the 2-char floor is loose and a false positive costs a duplicate push). Validate against the real Ink TUI, not the fixture: test/fixtures/dispatch-geometry/raw-echo.ts models wrap behaviour that has already been wrong once (it encoded eager downward wrap until US-R1-001 corrected it).

SCOPE. Replace the tail-matching backstop with the prompt-row discriminator; correct the overclaiming module header and the `composerLineRetainsPayloadTail` doc comment; add a real-tmux regression test driving a TRAILING-SPACE payload at the exact wrap boundary (len 77 at width 80) asserting NOT delivered plus a retry, which is the case no current test covers.

CONSTRAINT (unchanged from CAM-359). Correct in BOTH directions: a delivered payload must not be resent (duplicate sends trip the back-to-back send-keys race, scripts/cam/patterns.md:330) and an undelivered one must not read as delivered.

PRIORITY NOTE. Narrow residue (payload must end in a space AND land exactly on a wrap boundary), and CAM-359 already removed the far larger always-delivered-for-any-wrapped-payload defect. Filed so the gap is tracked rather than silently carried under a comment claiming it is closed.
